items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in a field relevant to disabilities and higher education, such as social work, counseling, psychology, educational psychology, education, rehabilitation counseling or related field or any combination of education and experience that provides the required knowledge, skills and ability to perform the job.
Three years’ experience working in a higher education setting, or a combination of relevant professional and higher education experience preferred.
At least two years of experience working with student disability support services, preferred.
Provide academic coaching and services to a diverse and talented student population.
Manage a caseload of students as designated by the AVPSA.
Support the Office of Accommodations and Academic Resource Services in support of identified students with accommodations, and other areas of need.
Document and maintain case records.
Ensure timely responses to inquiries from all constituencies.
Maintain the confidentiality of student records as required by law and College policy.
Gather and report necessary data for assessment purposes.
Serve as a point of contact for students, which includes student outreach, resource referral, faculty and staff liaison, and general consultation.
Develop partnerships with campus and consortia supportive resources to promote academic success and retention.
Hire, train, and supervise tutor coordinators, and other student employees hired by the Office of AARS.
Work collaboratively with CARE@Scripps and the Case Management office.
Where appropriate, provide training, guidance, and support to faculty and/or staff working with students being supported by Academic Resource Services.
Organize, plan, and execute the academic coaching program including initiatives, including topics such as time management, learning strategies, reading enhancement, and organization.
Work with students who have received low grade notices or are on academic probation to provide academic support services.
Assist with marketing tasks related to programs with Academic Resource Services.
Participate in weekly staff meetings.
Active support for the College’s Principles of Community and Institutional Values.

Student Affairs staff perform critical functions with regard to the operation of the College, which looks to Student Affairs professionals to support students in a dynamic and ever-evolving campus environment.
Strong advising and interpersonal skills.
Excellent verbal and written communications skills.
Ability to work effectively with a diverse population of students, faculty, and staff.
Ability to help students develop optimal learning skills and present training and motivational programs to a wide variety of groups.
Ability to handle multiple responsibilities and tasks simultaneously in a busy environment.
Must possess tact and exercise sound judgment in dealing with sensitive and/or confidential matters.
